prompt:
A cost anomaly was detected in a cloud billing dataset. Your job is root cause analysis: identify the resource(s) responsible for the anomalous cost change.

Anomaly details (from anomaly.json, also in your working directory):
{
    "date": "2025-10-13",
    "account_id": "CZ4NH6K"
}

The file data.csv in your working directory contains the daily cost data for the accounts. Investigate it with code (inspect the columns first) and determine which resource(s) caused the anomalous cost for this account on this date. A resource is identified by its name (the exact value as it appears in data.csv) and its type (the data.csv column that value comes from, written in title case with spaces instead of underscores, e.g. a value from a column named some_column has type "Some Column").

Recommended method (aim to finish in about 6-8 tool calls):
1. Inspect the columns and filter to the anomalous account. Compare the anomaly date with a baseline of the preceding normal days.
2. For EVERY categorical column (not only one), compute the cost change per value between the baseline and the anomaly date. Do this for all columns in a single tool call.
3. Decide which column is the root-cause dimension: the one whose values explain the total cost change most fully and most specifically. A change in one column often shows up indirectly in other columns, so compare the columns before choosing; do not assume a particular column.
4. The root cause can be one value or many values of that column. Include every value that materially drives the change, and nothing else.
5. Answer.

Required final answer format (JSON inside <answer></answer> tags):
{"resource": [{"name": "<resource name>", "type": "<resource type>"}]}
List every resource that is a root cause; include only root causes.

import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
acc = df[df.account_id=='CZ4NH6K'].copy()
anom = acc[acc.date=='10/13/25']
base_dates = ['10/9/25','10/10/25','10/11/25','10/12/25']
base = acc[acc.date.isin(base_dates)]

# residual after removing the two instance families
a = anom[~anom.instance_family.isin(['HRNHGYQxfj','vhnT3Q7AY2'])]
b = base[~base.instance_family.isin(['HRNHGYQxfj','vhnT3Q7AY2'])]
print('residual total change:', a.unblended_cost.sum() - b.groupby('date')['unblended_cost'].sum().mean())

# per cloud_service change in residual
a2 = a.groupby('cloud_service')['unblended_cost'].sum()
b2 = b.groupby('cloud_service')['unblended_cost'].mean()
print((a2-b2).sort_values(ascending=False).round(2))

# check if cloud_service -> csp is fixed
print(acc.groupby('cloud_service')['csp'].nunique())
# check application -> cloud_service fixed?
print(acc.groupby('application')['cloud_service'].nunique().value_counts())
# check instance_family -> cloud_service/application fixed?
print(acc.groupby('instance_family')['cloud_service'].nunique().value_counts())
print(acc.groupby('instance_family')['application'].nunique().value_counts())

import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
acc = df[df.account_id=='CZ4NH6K'].copy()
anom = acc[acc.date=='10/13/25']
base_dates = ['10/9/25','10/10/25','10/11/25','10/12/25']
base = acc[acc.date.isin(base_dates)]

famset = ['HRNHGYQxfj','vhnT3Q7AY2']
a = anom[~anom.instance_family.isin(famset)]
b = base[~base.instance_family.isin(famset)]
print('residual total change:', round(a.unblended_cost.sum() - b.groupby('date')['unblended_cost'].sum().mean(),2))

# per application change in residual
a2 = a.groupby('application')['unblended_cost'].sum()
b2 = b.groupby('application')['unblended_cost'].mean()
ch = (a2-b2).sort_values(ascending=False)
print(ch.round(2).to_string())

# per instance_family change in residual
a3 = a.groupby('instance_family')['unblended_cost'].sum()
b3 = b.groupby('instance_family')['unblended_cost'].mean()
ch3 = (a3-b3).sort_values(ascending=False)
print(ch3.head(15).round(2).to_string())
print('n instance families in residual:', len(ch3))

# num_instances check for the two fams on anomaly vs base
for fam in famset:
    print(fam, 'anom num:', anom[anom.instance_family==fam].num_instances.sum(),
          'base avg num:', round(base[base.instance_family==fam].groupby('date')['num_instances'].sum().mean(),2))
